text:
hari: Heads-up — onboarding Mistral-lite v0.3 (q4 int4) onto staging produced localized regressions in CJK and RTL evals. zh->en BLEU baseline (fp16) 29.9 -> mistral-int4 25.4 on bench/xx_to_en_1k. ar->en ~ -3.8 BLEU. Need triage.
hari: Repro command I used:
```
# snapshot: mistral-2026-04-12
python eval/translate.py --model mistral-lite-v0.3 --quant int4 --dataset bench/xx_to_en_1k.jsonl --batch 32
```
hari: Quick failing snippet (Chinese):
```
src: 他说：“我去。”
fp16: He said, "I'll go."
int4: He said , " I ' ll go . "
```
hari: Arabic example has nested parentheses and embedded english acronym, bracket order flips and missing RLI/LRI marks.

nora: Could be detok/normalization in the int4 fast path. Any kernel tag on the canary?

buildbot: deploy-bot: Canary build for mistral-int4 used kernel tag `kernels/normalize/fast-norm-lite-2026-04-11` deployed 2026-04-11T22:07Z. Tokenizer package unchanged.

kevin: I dumped tokenization+detok traces for a few failing examples. Token ids match for short snippets, but detok log shows repeated messages: `norm: collapsed U+200D` and `norm: removed U+2067` and `norm: inserted_space_before U+3002`.

yasmin: Collapsing ZWJ (U+200D) or removing RLI (U+2067) explains the CJK joiner and RTL isolation breaks. Inserting space before IDEOGRAPHIC FULL STOP (U+3002) explains stray space problems.

kevin: Example token ids for chinese snippet:
``
fp16 ids: [1200,3322,44,77,9002]
int4 ids: [1200,3322,44,77,9002]
```
kevin: But detok diffs show non-idempotent behavior only on int4 kernel.

nora: Quick mitigation: re-run int4 with TEXT_NORMALIZE=compat-preserve or runtime flag `--unicode-preserve`. If BLEU recovers, kernel normalization policy is the root cause.

kevin: Running compatibility run now, ETA ~12m.

# status update
kevin: Compat-preserve run completed: zh->en BLEU = 29.7, ar->en back within 0.2 pts of fp16. So this reproduces.

yasmin: Good. Root cause confirmed: `fast-norm-lite-2026-04-11` is collapsing/stripping control codepoints and applying ideographic spacing heuristics. That's too aggressive for multilingual defaults.

hari: Action items: @nora open kernel issue with minimal repros and detok logs, @kevin add a test fixture to eval harness (`eval/fixtures/zwc_bidi_cjk_mistral.jsonl`) with targeted cases for ZWJ/ZWNJ/RLI/LRI and ideographic punctuation spacing, @yasmin prepare rollback PR to pin mistral-int4 to `kernels/normalize/stable-2026-03`.

nora: Opening issue now, attaching repros and a short trace; issue #4512. Proposed patch: make fast-norm opt-in and preserve control chars by default for models with multilingual coverage.

buildbot: deploy-bot: Rollback to `kernels/normalize/stable-2026-03` started at 2026-04-12T02:55Z for canary group mistral-canary-1.

yasmin: I'll kick off rollback canary smoke and then run a full regression.

kevin: Added fixture and a small gating test; pushing PR to eval harness. Also added a quick smoke that fails if detok log contains `removed U+200D` or `removed U+2067` for any multilingual fixture.

hari: Longer-term: we should add a telemetry metric counting dropped control codepoints per model/quant and a canary gate threshold. If any non-zero drops for multilingual regions, fail canary.

yasmin: Agreed. Also adding a customer-facing runtime flag for "aggressive-ascii-normalize" so customers who only need ascii flows can opt-in. Default remains preserve for safety.

kevin: One oddity: a few longer Chinese sentences still show token boundary jitter after rollback but that's in the noise; I'll run TTest across the full eval suite.

hari: Thanks everyone. Keep updates in-thread and tag me on PRs. :thumbsup:
